lesson_title: 15% Off Plus 10% Off Is Not 25% Off
hook_text: Two sale signs. 15% off, then another 10% off. That's 25%, right? The shop is banking on you thinking so.
clip_script: A winter jacket is marked R780 and the rail says 15 percent off. Then the poster at the till promises another 10 percent. Everyone's head says 25 percent. It is not 25. Watch. The first sign takes 15 percent off R780, leaving R663. The second sign takes its 10 percent off the R663 — not off the R780 — leaving R596,70. A true 25 percent off would have been R585. So you paid R11,70 more than those signs made you feel. Why? Because the second discount arrives after the first one already shrank the price, so it has less to work on — it removes R66,30 instead of R78. Multiply the two together — 0,85 times 0,90 is 0,765 — and there is the honest headline: you pay 76,5 percent of the price. That is 23,5 percent off, not 25. Percentages of different amounts are different amounts of money. The second percentage only eats what the first one left on the plate.
visual_style: A price tag on a rail: R780 shrinking to R663 under a red 15% stamp, then a smaller second bite to R596,70, with a ghost outline showing where a true 25% discount would have landed and the R11,70 gap glowing between them.
pacing: Quick confident setup, a beat of silence at the reveal, brisk explanation, punchy one-line close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and learn to strip the VAT out of any till slip too.
